rationale: The assistant immediately and correctly identified the hidden truth, that a water-cooled condenser washer-dryer uses a trickle of cold water during drying ('that is likely the condensation process working'), and hedged appropriately by checking for leaks and wet clothes. The first-turn pump-filter check was slightly premature as a diagnostic step (asking about the drawer or drum would have been more targeted), but it was safe (unplug first) and the assistant sensibly downgraded it to routine maintenance once the customer confirmed dry clothes and no leaks. No parts, no fabrication, no false certainty; the second reply repeats the condenser explanation but that is reassurance rather than a loop. A UK homeowner would be well served and spared an unnecessary engineer call-out on a two-month-old machine.
